I've been thinking about Alice telling the Caterpillar she's changed several times since morning, Pinocchio promising the Fairy he'd be back in an hour and then dawdling with Lamp-Wick anyway, and Keller forgetting all about college at the lake. Put them next to that Hume passage and what I wrote about work versus old friends. Is there a way to see both sides of me without calling either one fake?

I've been thinking about Alice telling the Caterpillar she's changed several times since morning, Pinocchio promising the Fairy he'd be back in an hour and then dawdling with Lamp-Wick anyway, and Keller forgetting all about college at the lake. Put them next to that Hume passage and what I wrote about work versus old friends. Honestly, part of me hopes they show that a different mood makes me a different person, so I'm not really bound to host next month. Do they?

I keep coming back to that idea that we're just a bundle of perceptions. I'm a different person at work than with my old friends. And the thing I said I'd host next month: every time something more fun comes up, I tell myself one more day of not preparing won't matter. Does anything I've read speak to that pull without making one side of me fake?

Something in sectionals today sent me straight back to The Story of My Life, to Helen at the well-house with the water running over her hand. Aina, one of my Sec 1 flautists, has been miscounting the same rhythms since January, and this afternoon she suddenly clapped a dotted pattern perfectly and looked up at me as if a light had come on. I had more or less filed her under slow, and I'm a bit ashamed of that now. How do I keep faith with the beginners who haven't had their moment yet, on the days when the repetition feels like it's doing nothing?
My new neighbour Dario asked whether he could come along to supper club. Which night did I tell you I host it now, and what did I say it used to be?
I've found three new recipes and I'm tempted to put all of them on the supper club menu this week. Have I tried something like this before, and how did it go?
I still get jittery at the start of the evening, right when everyone is watching me bring the food in. Did I ever find something that helped?
Dario has offered to bring a dessert. Have I mentioned anyone who can't eat something, so I can warn him?
